title: Chinese Historical Rulers Corpus — Canonical Master
purpose: Canonical denominator for all rulers/traditional sovereign figures to research or distill; completeness is never inferred from existing skills.
principle: Maximize historically relevant sovereign coverage first; represent uncertainty with orthogonal evidence/status fields instead of silently excluding difficult cases.

historical_core_required: highest decision-maker of a politically autonomous entity, sovereign polity, or competing central government
observable rule/control or institutionally recognized supreme-rule episode rather than pure posthumous honor
inclusion_rule.legendary_rule: Named traditional sovereign/culture-ruler figures enter LEGENDARY rather than being discarded; legendary status must never be presented as historical certainty.
default_exclusions: purely posthumous ruler with no lifetime rule episode
unsupported claimant with no governing entity
ordinary regional warlord without sovereign or central-government supreme-rule episode
deity with no meaningful ruler tradition
inclusion_rule.low_evidence_policy: Keep qualifying figures but mark LIMITED-EVIDENCE; never fabricate mental models to fill a quota.

corpus_layers.CORE: historically attested qualifying sovereign/highest rulers under the common rule
corpus_layers.EXTENDED: borderline autonomous regimes, exceptional de facto rulers, or analytically valuable edge cases
corpus_layers.LEGENDARY: traditional/legendary sovereign figures; included in maximal master but excluded from historical CORE completion denominator

completion_rule.historical_core: matched existing/distilled CORE persons / all CORE persons
completion_rule.maximal_master: CORE + EXTENDED + LEGENDARY tracked separately; never collapse legendary figures into historical completion percentage
completion_rule.identity: one person is counted once even when multiple titles, regimes, or rule episodes exist

enumeration_policy: Use multiple chronological/ruler-list sources and take their union before exclusions.
Never exclude merely because a regime is non-orthodox, defeated, short-lived, parallel, or uses a non-imperial title.
For Spring-Autumn/Warring States and fragmentation eras, enumerate polity-by-polity rather than sampling famous rulers.
For legendary traditions, preserve competing genealogies/lists as variants rather than forcing false consensus.
Every exclusion from a source-derived candidate set must have an explicit exclusion reason.
next_build_step: Enumerate every candidate person polity-by-polity into persons[], normalize aliases/duplicate identities, record exclusions, then machine-match against corpus-registry and skills paths.
